sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: CUSMA/USMCA — Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (in force 1 July 2020)
CETA — Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement
CPTPP — Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership
Canada-China Agreement for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (FIPA, in force 1 October 2014)
Canada-US Income Tax Convention (1980, as amended) and bilateral tax treaty network

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Alberta private corporations are governed by the Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended by the Business Corporations Amendment Act, 2022 (Bill 81), which requires filing of individuals with significant control (ISC) data with the Alberta Corporate Registry; the federal Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, ss 21.1-21.4, applies if a federal charter is chosen. AML/CFT obligations arise under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, and Regulations SOR/2002-184; sanctions and terrorist financing screening arise under the United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2, Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17, Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2017, c 21, and Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, Part II.1.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of beneficial owner's passport and proof of residential address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or equivalent competent authority in the document's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Canada's accession effective 11 January 2024); consular legalization by the Canadian mission where the origin country is not an Apostille member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incumbency of ultimate corporate shareholder (where UBO is a company)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or authorized corporate agent in the home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney for signatory/agent authorized to file Alberta incorporation documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the grantor's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source-of-funds bank reference letter for initial share capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Investor's issuing bank or financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank KYC channel; notarization/apostille required only if requested by the receiving bank or AML compliance officer

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-filing screening of every director, officer, shareholder and UBO against: OFAC SDN list; UN Security Council consolidated list; Canada's consolidated autonomous sanctions list under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; Criminal Code terrorist entity list; and internal adverse-media watchlists. Politically exposed persons (foreign, domestic and international-organization) are identified and risk-rated per the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; any PEP or sanctions hit triggers enhanced due diligence and escalating approval prior to incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES) via Service Alberta; mandatory NUANS (Newly Upgraded Name Search) corporate name search report
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: An Alberta corporate name must contain a distinctive element, a descriptive element, and a legal element ('Limited', 'Incorporated', 'Corporation' or abbreviations, or French equivalents). Names must be expressed in Roman (English/French) characters; non-Roman script names must be transliterated to the Latin alphabet. Prohibited punctuation and misleading/merely descriptive terms are screened through the NUANS report.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: canada (prominent distinctive use requires ministerial consent)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On NUANS rejection, the applicant should refile a revised name with a fresh NUANS report through the Alberta Corporate Registry, or submit a written reconsideration request to the Registrar within 30 days attaching existing-name-holder consent, trade-mark registrations, or explanatory submissions. If the Registrar confirms refusal, judicial review may be sought by application to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9; reserving an alternative distinctive name is the most expedient remediation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office with a physical street address in Alberta is acceptable as the registered office provided it maintains business hours, accepts service of process, and is not a bare post-office box. For subscription-box e-commerce, no local warehouse or physical premises is required at Stage 1; third-party fulfilment is permitted.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approx. 10%): unannounced on-site inspections by the Corporate Registry or CRA are uncommon for low-risk subscription retail absent tax/AML filing inconsistencies, consumer complaints, or sanctions/PEP flags.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (authorized NUANS service providers)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Incorporation filing fee — Alberta Business Corporation (standard electronic filing)
Notarization and Hague apostille/consular legalization of UBO identity and incumbency documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Home-country notary public and competent legalization authority

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certificate of Good Standing of ultimate corporate shareholder (with apostille, where applicable)
Registered office / corporate records address — annual virtual physical address service in Alberta
PEP, sanctions and adverse-media screening per director/UBO (OFAC, UN, Canada Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions List, Criminal Code list)
Preparation and filing of articles of incorporation, organizational resolutions, ISC/UBO register, minute book, and share certificates
Legal opinion on corporate capacity for Stripe Billing / Authorize.Net merchant onboarding

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss 1-17, 6-8 and 10 (articles, certificate, registered office, first directors)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (online: alberta.ca/corporate-registry; mail: Corporate Registry, 1020 - 106 Street, Edmonton, AB T5J 1H8, Canada)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) under s 6 of the ABCA, with Form 2 Notice of Registered Office and Form 3 Notice of First Directors
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital for an Alberta business corporation; no escrow capital account required at incorporation. Shares may be without par value and may be issued for any consideration permitted by the directors.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the incorporators' share subscription be accepted and full consideration received; that the shares issued in accordance with the articles. That the registered office of the Corporation be and is hereby established at [address], Alberta, in accordance with the Notice of Registered Office. That the following officers be appointed: [name] President, [name] Secretary-Treasurer, each to serve until replaced by resolution of the Board of Directors. That the Certificate of Incorporation be received and recorded in the corporate minute book. All acts and actions associated with these resolutions are ratified and confirmed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry / NUANS search platform (Service Alberta online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a NUANS name search through an accredited provider or via the Alberta Corporate Registry when using online incorporation. Submit a name reservation if the corporation is not yet ready to file articles. Verify that the proposed name is distinctive and includes a legal element such as 'Inc.' or 'Corp.'. The name reservation is valid for 90 days.
required_dossiers: NUANS Name Search Report
Certificate or government-issued ID of the incorporator
Proposed corporate name in English (or bilingual), with alternative names if desired
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused as confusingly similar or contrary to s 11(3) of the ABCA, file a revised name search with a fresh primary name and application; a reserved name may be amended before the incorporation is completed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and File Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (online filing through Service Alberta; paper submissions to Corporate Registry, Edmonton)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Duly execute Form 1 Articles of Incorporation (share structure, class rights, restrictions) and attach Form 2 Notice of Registered Office and Form 3 Notice of First Directors. File online or send the signed paper copy to the registry. Pay the applicable statutory fee. The Articles must set out the corporation's name, share structure, and any limitations on transferee rights. The first directors' consents and registered office consent are required.
required_dossiers: Completed and signed Form 1
Form 2 Notice of Registered Office
Form 3 Notice of First Directors
Consents of first directors (or included in Form 3)
Proof of applicable name reservation/NUANS report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry returns a defect or query, review the notice and refile correct information promptly (typically within 20 days); if the period lapses, re-submit the entire incorporation with a new payment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Incorporation and Initial Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (certificate issuance after approval of Articles)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon acceptance, the Registry issues a Certificate of Incorporation in electronic or hard-copy form. Verify corporate name, number, and date of incorporation. Request a certified copy or corporate profile for banking and licensing if needed. The board should then open a corporate minute book and record initial share subscriptions and officer appointments.
required_dossiers: Registry receipt / filing confirmation
Certificate of Incorporation
Corporate profile or attestation, if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains an error, file an application with the Corporate Registry for re-issuance under s 6(3) of the ABCA; if still not received, call the Registry support desk and provide proof of payment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register Business Number (BN) and Tax Accounts with CRA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency – Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Certificate of Incorporation, open a CRA Business Registry (My Business Account) and apply online for a Business Number (BN), GST/HST account (mandatory if the corporation's taxable annual revenues exceed CAD 30,000), corporate income tax account, and discretionary payroll account if employees will be hired. The corporation must also register for the Alberta provincial corporate tax (administered by CRA on behalf of Alberta).
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Form RC59 (Business Consent Authorization)
Personal name/residential address and government-issued ID of authorized director
Corporate registered office address and mailing address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA registration is delayed or denied, complete a paper Form RC1 and file by mail with evidence of the incorporation; call the CRA business enquiry line for escalation and obtain a temporary BN.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for Municipal Business Licence and Zoning Compliance (if physical premises)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Calgary – Business Licensing and Permits; or equivalent municipal licensing office for the applicable location
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the corporation operates from an office, warehouse, or fulfilment centre, apply for a municipal business licence under the Business Licence Bylaw. Submit the corporate profile/certificate, premises floor plan, and proof of zoning/development permit. The licence fee is determined based on the business activity and square footage. Renew the licence annually.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and corporate registry search
Municipal business licence application form
Site/floor plan of the premises
Zoning clearance or development permit (if change of use)
Safety inspection certificate (if required by the fire department)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is refused due to zoning, apply to the zoning board for a variance or seek relocation; if rejected for non-compliance, remedy the identified defect and appeal within 14 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Municipal Affairs – Business and Consumer Services (no mandatory industry licence for subscription box retailing); applicable municipal business licensing office for premises
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No compulsory operating licence; optional municipal business licence (e.g., 'Retail / E-Commerce Wholesale Business Licence') for physical locations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – subscription box warehousing/packaging is not an activity listed in Schedule 1 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Regulation (AR 130/2001); no EIA report or registration required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For non-hazardous solid waste, comply with the Waste Control Regulation (AR 192/1996) and municipal collection bylaws; no air emissions or VOC thresholds apply; no industrial wastewater discharge; any sanitary sewage to municipal system is permitted under the local drainage bylaw. If using aerosol or solvent-based packaging, relevant VOC limits under the Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives are not exceeded.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification may be required from the local fire authority under the Alberta Fire Code (AR 146/2021) for a warehouse or office (fire extinguishers, exit signage, sprinklers for high-density storage). Occupational health and safety clearance under the Alberta OHS Code is mandatory if employees are engaged; a preliminary hazard assessment and first aid supplies are required. For racked storage, a structural load check and warehouse safety inspection are advised.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal taxes and Alberta Treasury Board and Finance / Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration Division for provincial taxes; primary portal CRA My Business and Alberta government tax portals
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Canadian corporations obtain a nine-digit Business Number (BN) directly from the CRA website by completing the online business registration form; subsequent GST/HST registration via Form GST400 if taxable supplies exceed the threshold; Alberta provincial corporate tax filings commence after BN issuance with no separate federal TIN required beyond the BN
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections or hybrid mismatch elections available; Canadian tax classification is determined exclusively by the legal form of incorporation as a business corporation

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: $30,000 CAD annual taxable supplies in Canada
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All GST/HST registrants must file returns and remit tax electronically through the CRA My Business portal; real-time fiscal clearance not mandated but digital invoicing systems with audit trails are required for compliance; no mandatory digital stamping for every transaction

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: GST is zero-rated on exports of goods from Canada and on supplies of qualifying services to non-residents outside Canada; eligibility requires the supply to qualify as an export supply, proof of export or delivery to non-resident, and timely remittance of any applicable taxes
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent zero-rating claims trigger penalties up to 200 percent of the GST amount, interest charges, and potential criminal prosecution under the Excise Tax Act; retrospective GST assessments and full clawbacks apply for non-compliance with documentation requirements

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada / Banque du Canada
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible with no exchange controls on current or capital account transactions. Profit remittance, dividend repatriation, capital injections, loan repaayments and trade-related payments are all freely transferrable without central-bank pre-approval. The only statutory constraints are standard taxation compliance (dividend withholding under the Income Tax Act) and FINTRAC reporting thresholds. Canada operates a floating exchange rate regime; there is no restriction on holding foreign currency domestically or abroad.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement in Canada. Exporters are not obliged to repatriate foreign-currency receipts within any timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio applies. The government only requires statistical reporting to Statistics Canada (BOP reporting), and FINTRAC large-cash or suspicious-transaction reporting for high-value trade settlements; underlying commercial invoices, customs and banking records remain the primary compliance evidence.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. Non-bank fintechs operating as payment service providers in Canada must register under the Retail Payment Activities Act with the Bank of Canada and must safeguard funds. Foreign EMIs must also be registered extra-provincially in Alberta and maintain Canadian representation. Such providers can support subscription-billing rails and FX conversion but cannot accept deposits or provide escrow-grade custodial services; a Schedule I bank account remains the required spine for treasury and capital escrow.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence in Canada is mandatory at the corporate registry level; a registered office and Alberta agent are legally required. For account onboarding, most Schedule I banks now allow remote opening using notarized or apostilled corporate documents, but for non-resident directors and foreign-parent ownership, an in-person or video interview with the authorized signatory is standard practice. A full documentary corporate KYC package, including a certified corporate search, register of directors, UBO declaration and source-of-funds evidence, is mandated; pure online onboarding of non-resident Capital Escrow Accounts is uncommon.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of complete ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) documentation for the corporate shareholder chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta Corporate Registry certified extracts, Articles of Incorporation, register of directors and shareholders, full organizational chart, beneficial-owner declarations for every shareholder holding 10% or more, and clean RCMP criminal-record confirmation for senior officers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident director or authorized signatory resident in a jurisdiction with fragmented AML enforcement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized or apostilled government-issued passport copy, certificate of incumbency, a current bank reference letter from the director's primary bank, RCMP criminal-history check, and a formal board resolution naming the director as agent for bank-opening purposes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Subscription-commerce profile flagged as high-chargeback aggregate payment processing rather than a physical goods retailer
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PCI DSS Level 1 attestation, Stripe or Authorize.Net transaction and settlement ledgers for the most recent operating period, published refund and cancellation policies, chargeback monitoring procedures, and a specimen subscription agreement with transparent billing terms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound equity injection from a foreign parent in a grey-listed or opaque beneficial-ownership jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Parent-company audited financial statements, bank statements covering six months, board resolutions authorising the capital injection, signed subscription or shareholder loan agreement, CRS/FATCA self-certifications, and documented economic nexus with Alberta fulfilment operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ISIC 4791 classification misinterpreted as an online payment-intermediary or financial-service merchant rather than a product subscription business
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Third-party warehouse lease, duty-paid import invoices and customs B3 forms, final-mile carrier contracts, sample product packaging and branding photographs, and customer-order tracking data demonstrating physical merchandise movement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 from the foreign parent's bank, with beneficiary bank BIC and the subscriber's unique operational account number in field 59. Put 'EQUITY INJECTION CA_CORP' or 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN DISBURSEMENT' in field 70, and match each wire to a board resolution, subscription agreement or intercompany loan note. For USD, route through RBC/TD/CIBC correspondent banking or Fedwire settlement; for other currencies, onshore spot conversion through the account bank's FX desk is required. Statistics Canada and FINTRAC reporting is handled by the bank, but the corporate treasury must keep the underlying capital-file complete from the first credit date.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier settlements for imported box contents should use SWIFT MT103 for recurring low-value invoices, irrevocable confirmed letters of credit (LC) issued by a Schedule I Canadian bank for bulk stock purchases, and intercompany cross-border transfers tied to arm's-length contracts. All disbursements must be paired with supplier invoices, bills of lading, packing lists and customs documentation for CRA tax deductibility. Customer refunds flow out via Stripe Billing or Authorize.Net through the merchant settlement account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forwards (USD/CAD and major pairs)
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for restricted or exotic cross pairs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Government of Alberta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the anniversary date of incorporation (or first registration date) of the company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a CAD $100 penalty if filed more than 30 days after the anniversary date; continued non-filing leads to administrative strike-off (dissolution) of the company after approximately one year of default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the corporation's fiscal year (e.g., for a December 31 year-end, filing due by June 30 of the following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty equals 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months (minimum CAD $100 if tax is owing and no return filed); interest accumulates on unpaid balances; repeated non-filing may trigger arbitrary assessment and asset-based collection measures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A corporation must appoint an independent auditor unless all shareholders (including non-voting) adopt a unanimous consent resolution annually exempting the appointment. No mandatory audit threshold exists for non-distributing companies; however, a distributing (public) company cannot waive the audit requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (required for publicly accountable entities) or ASPE (Canadian GAAP applicable to private enterprises) may be used; a non-distributing corporation may choose either framework consistently.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The corporation must maintain an Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register. Prior to filing the Annual Return, the company must review and update the register to reflect any changes in significant control. Any change must be recorded in the register within 15 days after the company becomes aware of it. The Annual Return includes a confirmation that the ISC register is accurate and up to date.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 100 to 300 per year for registered office and registered agent services in Alberta
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 to 15,000 per year for a statutory audit, depending on entity size, transactions, and audit complexity; a shareholder waiver eliminates this expense.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined headline corporate income tax rate: 15% federal Part I general rate (38% base rate less 10% provincial abatement less 13% General Rate Reduction) plus 8% Alberta general corporate income tax rate applicable to a corporation resident in Canada; a non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada through a permanent establishment in Alberta is taxable on Canadian-source business income at the same 23% combined rate.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Canadian-Controlled Private Corporation (CCPC) Small Business Deduction: combined 11% rate (federal 9% + Alberta 2%) on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income within the respective federal and Alberta business limits; Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) refundable Investment Tax Credit of 35% on qualifying expenditures up to CAD 3,000,000 for CCPCs (15% non-refundable credit above the ceiling and for other corporations); no Alberta capital tax and no federal capital tax; Alberta imposes no provincial sales tax (only 5% GST), preserving platform cost basis for subscription-box fulfilment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form T2 – Corporation Income Tax Return (federal and Alberta integrated return); filed electronically via CRA E-File / NETFILE through approved commercial tax software or a registered tax preparer's E-File portal; accessed through CRA 'My Business Account' for corporate taxpayers.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; balance of tax due instalment obligations are due quarterly for corporations with federal plus Alberta tax payable exceeding CAD 3,000 in the current or preceding tax year (monthly instalments apply to large corporations).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 must be filed within six calendar months after the fiscal year-end; for a December 31, 2025 fiscal year-end, the statutory deadline is June 30, 2026. Final remaining balance of Part I tax is due no later than two months after the fiscal year-end for most corporations and three months for CCPCs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Cover – Corporation Name and Business Number (BN)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name as registered under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) or the Canada Business Corporations Act, and the nine-digit CRA Business Number with the CRA corporate income tax program account.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Canadian-incorporated subsidiary of a foreign parent, enter the exact Canadian registered legal name; the foreign parent is not named on the T2 cover. For a non-resident corporation with a Canadian permanent establishment, the same BN is used and the head office address in the resident jurisdiction is disclosed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Date of the corporate taxation year-end; the first fiscal period cannot exceed 53 weeks after incorporation; subsequent fiscal periods must be aligned to a consistent annual date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a foreign-owned Canadian subsidiary, the Canadian fiscal year-end should match the accounting reference period of the audited financial statements prepared in Canada; divergent foreign group fiscal periods require a Canadian standalone stub-period filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Designation of Alberta as the province in which the corporation has a permanent establishment; taxable income is allocated among provinces using the T2 permanent establishment allocation schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Canadian subsidiary whose operational headquarters, fulfilment warehouse, and managerial control are in Alberta allocates 100% of taxable income to Alberta; a non-resident corporation must complete the PE allocation schedule for the Alberta PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross subscription-box revenue, including periodic subscription fees and one-off box purchases, before any deductions; GST/HST (5% in Alberta) is excluded from revenue reported for income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Canadian-source revenue for a non-resident carrying on business in Canada; a Canadian-resident corporation reports worldwide gross revenue. Reconcile gross settlements from Stripe Billing and Authorize.Net to the line amount; payment processor fees are not netted here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs of inventory, product packaging, inbound freight, customs duties, and directly attributable fulfilment labour required to assemble subscription boxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Costs allocable to the Canadian PE are deductible if incurred in Canada or for goods consumed in Canada; intercompany purchases from a foreign related supplier must be arm's-length and documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part 1 – Line 320 (Operating, General, and Administrative Expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Marketing, software and payment-processing fees (including Stripe Billing and Authorize.Net merchant discounts), warehouse rent, employee salaries, professional fees, and other deductible operating outlays subject to the Income Tax Act reasonableness limitation (s. 67).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Head-office management fees and foreign-parent IT charges are deductible only if arm's-length and substantiated; otherwise Part I disallowance and Part XIII withholding on deemed fees apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income before Part I provisions after adding back non-deductible disbursements (fines, penalties, 50% of most business meals, non-arm's-length unreasonable portions) and after capital loss and/or non-capital loss carryforward applications.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The taxpayer must apply the 20-year non-capital loss carryforward period and the three-year carryback election; foreign tax credits from foreign-source subscription IP licensing are calculated in Schedule 21, not as a deduction on this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part 1 – Line 360 (Federal Tax on Taxable Income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal Part I tax computed at 15% general rate or 9% CCPC business rate, after 10% abatement and 13% General Rate Reduction, before investment tax credits and other refundable credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Canadian subsidiary wholly owned by a non-resident is not a CCPC solely because of non-resident shareholding; the small business rate applies only if at least 50% of votes and value are held by Canadian residents and no more than 50% of income is from non-active business.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 – Alberta Corporate Tax Calculation (Provincial Schedule 500 Series)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of Alberta corporate income tax at 8% general rate or 2% small business rate on the Alberta-allocated portion of taxable income, integrated into the T2 return and remitted to the CRA.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident corporation with a PE in Alberta, the Alberta tax is computed only on income reasonably attributable to the Alberta PE; treaty PE thresholds (e.g., Canada-US Article V) may exempt the entity from Alberta tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of depreciation deductions for leasehold improvements, computer hardware, equipment, and software used in subscription-box operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: CCA allocable to the Canadian PE must relate to property used in that PE; foreign-owned assets used both abroad and in Canada must be allocated on a reasonable basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 125 – Income Statement and Balance Sheet
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Audited or internally prepared financial statements, including income statement, balance sheet, and statement of retained earnings, filed in the format prescribed by CRA.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Canadian subsidiary of a foreign group must file standalone Canadian financial statements; consolidated worldwide financial statements are not acceptable for Schedule 125; intercompany balances with the foreign parent must be separately identified.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the T2: penalty of 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per complete month late, maximum 12 months, where the return is filed late and tax is owing; repeated late filing in a subsequent year doubles the base penalty percentage. Arrears interest at the prescribed rate (currently approximately 8%-10% annual, set quarterly) compounds daily on unpaid balances. Failure to report income: repeated failure penalty of 10% of unpaid federal tax for the current and same class of the prior year; gross negligence penalty (s. 163(2)) of CAD 100 plus 50% of the understated tax on any misstatement due to culpable negligence. TP documentation penalty: 10% of the transfer-pricing adjustment, with no statutory cap.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form T106 – Information Return for Non-Arm's-Length Transactions with Non-Residents; filed through CRA E-File with the T2, or paper-filed with the T2 where E-File is unavailable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, for each taxation year in which the Canadian taxpayer has reportable non-arm's-length controlled transactions with a non-resident aggregate exceeding CAD 1,000,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T106 must be filed on or before the T2 filing deadline, i.e., within six months after the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part A – Identification of the Canadian Reporter and Foreign Related Parties
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The Canadian entity's BN, the legal name and tax jurisdiction of each non-resident related corporation or individual, and the relationship type.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign parent and all subsidiaries, together with any non-resident individual controlling the Canadian subsidiary, must be listed; incomplete identification of the ultimate parent can trigger automatic penalty assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Nature and amount of cross-border controlled transactions: purchases, sales, management fees, royalties, interest, and services paid or received.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a subscription-box corporation licensing IP, trademarks, or customer data from a foreign related party, each royalty stream and data-service fee must be reported separately; valuations of non-IP service bundles must be substantiated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part C – Transfer Pricing Method Selection
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selection of the most appropriate arm's-length methodology and the resulting income or loss allocation for each controlled transaction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The selected method must match the contemporaneous documentation prepared by the Canadian taxpayer; use of CUP for a subscription fee benchmark against comparable Boxable or Cratejoy-style markets is expected for standard merchandise.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part D – Penalty and Waiver Attestation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Whether the taxpayer made reasonable efforts to apply the arm's-length principle; signature and certification by the authorized corporate officer.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-controlled Canadian corporation must ensure the T106 is signed by an officer who can verify the TP documentation; the penalty relief for 'reasonable efforts' is unavailable if the return is filed late or incomplete.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file T106: CAD 100 per day per information return, minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500 per return, under s. 162(6); cumulative penalties can reach CAD 25,000 or more for multiple transactions; plus 10% TP adjustment penalty and gross negligence penalties where omissions are deliberate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: NR4 Return and NR4-B slips – Statement of Amounts Paid or Credited to Non-Residents of Canada; filed via CRA E-File or the CRA's 'My Business Account' portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual remittance; Part XIII withholding tax remittances are due monthly if the average monthly withheld amount exceeds CAD 500, quarterly if below that threshold; the NR4 annual summary is due March 31 of the calendar year following the calendar year in which the payments were made.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: NR4 summary and NR4-B slips must be filed on or before March 31 following the calendar year in which the payment was credited to the non-resident; the withholding tax itself is remitted monthly or quarterly under the prescribed schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The Canadian payer corporation's name, BN, and residency; identifies the payer as the statutory withholding agent under Part XIII.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Canadian subsidiary paying dividends to a non-resident parent, the subsidiary is the withholding agent; all amounts paid or credited to the non-resident parent during the calendar year must be aggregated on one NR4-B per parent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross amount of dividends, interest, royalties, rents, or other Part XIII subject amounts paid or credited to each non-resident.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treat royalties for subscription-box IP licensed from the foreign parent separately from dividends; substitution of royalty for dividend payments is high-risk and subject to recharacterization by CRA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of Part XIII tax withheld, normally 25% absent an approved treaty-reduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Treaty rate of 5% (parent owns at least 10% of Canadian subsidiary) or 15% (portfolio dividend) under Canada-US applies only when the foreign parent has submitted an approved NR302/NR301 form and current Tax Residency Certificate (TRC).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Citation of the applicable tax treaty article and the beneficial ownership entitlement supporting the reduced withholding rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: CRA requires the non-resident recipient to be the beneficial owner and to satisfy the treaty's limitation-on-benefits provision; a 'shell' foreign parent without substance will be denied treaty relief, and the Canadian subsidiary will be liable for the 25% deficiency.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to withhold: penalty under s. 227(9) of 10% of the amount not withheld; failure to remit: daily interest at prescribed rates on the unremitted amount; failure to file NR4: CAD 25 per day per slip, minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500; directors of the Canadian subsidiary are personally jointly and severally liable for unremitted Part XIII withholding under s. 227.1.
